papers.relied_on: Row 20 cites it as 2026 evidence that total insulin, C-peptide and insulin autoantibodies identify insulin autoimmune syndrome (IAS).
papers.full_text_shows: A 67-year-old man (China): 75 g OGTT with timed insulin and C-peptide gave fasting insulin 804 mU/L and >1,000 mU/L stimulated, with C-peptide 2.12 to 10.45 nmol/L; IAA 115.57 COI; imaging negative. PEG precipitation, dilution and heterophile blocking were not done, so the diagnosis rests on IAA and the insulin/C-peptide pattern. Pantoprazole causation is only suggested (clopidogrel confounder, prednisone given); the literature review has six PPI cases.
papers.quote: The interference testing (PEG precipitation, dilution linearity, and heterophile blocking) was not performed
papers.key_numbers: Fasting insulin 804 mU/L (hospital retest 75.20 mU/L, ref 3-25); fasting C-peptide 1.45 nmol/L; IAA 115.57 COI (ref <0.9); IAA normal after about 4 months; 6 PPI case reports reviewed
papers.role_in_work: Supporting case report for row 20 (IAS recognition by insulin, C-peptide and IAA)
papers.design: Single case report plus narrative literature review of 6 cases (no formal appraisal)
papers.measure_type: Post-load (OGTT with timed insulin and C-peptide) and spontaneous-hypoglycaemia insulin and C-peptide; insulin autoantibodies. Not mixed-meal.
papers.assay_or_platform: Electrochemiluminescence (first hospital) and chemiluminescence immunoassays; IAA by chemiluminescence; PEG not run
papers.quality_note: Case-level evidence; no PEG step; two assays gave very different insulin values (804 vs 75.2 mU/L); conflict-of-interest statement not located in the part read.

papers.relied_on: Row 20 cites it as a 2026 review supporting insulin, IAA and PEG testing to diagnose IAS.
papers.full_text_shows: Narrative review plus one case (76-year-old man, insulin 1126 uIU/mL, C-peptide 10.11 ng/mL, ALA 600 mg daily) and a 12-case ALA literature table. It calls IAA detection the cornerstone and PEG precipitation inexpensive and widely accessible, and states no standardized treatment guidelines exist; management rests on case reports and expert consensus. It cites a systematic review of 294 patients (56% remission with trigger removal and diet alone). Insulin-to-C-peptide ratio and insulin >1000 uIU/mL are only ancillary markers.
papers.quote: no standardized treatment guidelines are available for IAS, largely because of its rarity and the absence of randomized controlled trials
papers.key_numbers: Insulin often >100 and up to >=1000 uIU/mL; PEG: total vs supernatant insulin difference; 294-patient systematic review (secondary citation): 56% remission without immunosuppression; 12 ALA cases 2022-2026; 228 FAERS cases (secondary)
papers.role_in_work: Main narrative review supporting the row 20 diagnostic pathway
papers.design: Narrative review with one case report; no formal search protocol for the general part
papers.population_and_size: 1 case; 12 ALA cases tabulated; larger numbers are secondary citations
papers.measure_type: Total insulin and C-peptide at spontaneous hypoglycaemia, plus insulin autoantibodies and PEG precipitation; fasting or event-timed, not post-load
papers.assay_or_platform: Immunoassay (unspecified); PEG, gel filtration, mass spectrometry mentioned as alternatives
papers.quality_note: Narrative, case-based; no external funding; the review itself states no guideline exists. Supports Limited status; no diagnostic accuracy data.

papers.relied_on: Row 25 relies on it as the only source for PEG precipitation of maternal and infant samples when insulin is spuriously high; row 20 lists it as a supporting citation.
papers.full_text_shows: Narrative review (two authors, no conflicts declared) of transplacental maternal IAA, non-IAA IgG and neonatal IgM interfering with insulin and C-peptide immunoassays. It recommends PEG as a first-line test in neonatal hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia regardless of insulin or C-peptide level; a 20% fall after PEG (versus about 10% in controls) indicates antibodies. Frequency of assay-interfering antibodies is 0.5% (one prospective study, over 5,000 patients) up to 4% (retrospective), not specific to infants. No infant case counts, no accuracy data and no guideline support; the recommendation is the authors' own.
papers.quote: A PEG screening test precipitates all classes and subclasses of antibodies and should be included among first-line hormonal investigations.
papers.key_numbers: PEG: normal decline about 10%, 20% decline indicates antibodies (PEG 6000, 12.5% final); interference frequency 0.5% to 4% (general populations); no infant counts
papers.role_in_work: Sole source for row 25; side citation for row 20 (secondary IAS by maternal transfer)
papers.design: Narrative review with a worked Bayesian example; no search method
papers.measure_type: Insulin and C-peptide (random or critical sample, at hypoglycaemia) with PEG; not post-load
papers.assay_or_platform: Immunoassays generally (biotin-streptavidin and monoclonal designs discussed); PEG 6000; LC-MS as backup; no specific platform
papers.quality_note: Expert opinion, single group of authors, no primary data; recommendation not adopted by a guideline in the text read.

papers.text_quality: partial (PDF extraction; table and figure text partly garbled, numbers readable)
papers.relied_on: Row 21 cites it as a case report in which suppressed insulin and C-peptide pointed to NICTH.
papers.full_text_shows: A 96-year-old woman, glucose 38 mg/dL, 13x9x13 cm thoracic mass, insulin 0.5 U/mL (ref 1.8-12.2), C-peptide 0.03 ng/mL (ref 0.62-2.54), IGF-I 11 ng/mL. IGF-II was not measured, so the Doege-Potter label is 'suspected' and rests on suppressed insulin and C-peptide, the mass and low IGF-I. Dexamethasone resolved the hypoglycaemia; she died on day 16 of bacteraemia (attributed to translocation, not the tumour). The SFT had been biopsied elsewhere.
papers.quote: IGF-II was not measured in the present case because it was not available as a routine clinical assay
papers.key_numbers: Insulin 0.5 U/mL, C-peptide 0.03 ng/mL, IGF-I 11 ng/mL, glucose 38 mg/dL, mass 13 cm; hypoglycaemia in about 5-10% of SFT (cited)
papers.role_in_work: Illustrative case for row 21 (insulin and C-peptide suppression redirecting away from insulinoma)
papers.measure_type: Random insulin and C-peptide at hypoglycaemia (suppressed); no stimulated or post-load test
papers.quality_note: Case report; IGF-II confirmation missing, which is the confirmatory test in row 21; authors declare no conflict of interest.
